title: feat(knowledge-pgvector): a changed fingerprint builds a new generation and switches to it
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg3zXREECfPtgrM8TPQaxn1v)_

Fixes #37101

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读
- 用 PostgreSQL 存知识库的部署，换了嵌入模型或切分设置后，重建会在旧索引旁边建一套新索引，建好才切过去，旧的分批删掉；以前这种情况会拒绝重建、要运维手工清表。
- 属于「知识库平台」大项的第二阶段，替自建 PostgreSQL 的部署解决换模型后必须手工清索引的问题。
- 出错时最坏是重建期间该知识源检索一直返回「重建中」或旧索引未删干净占空间，不会返回新旧模型混排的错结果；这个包的改动可以直接撤回。
- 无。

## What changes

`@objectstack/knowledge-pgvector` builds a new generation beside the active one when the index fingerprint changes, and switches to it (ADR-0161 K7, rules 1 to 4). Before, `beginBuild` under a new fingerprint was refused and the reindex result carried hand-run SQL that cleared the source.

- **Generations.** The generation table holds one `active` and at most one `building` generation per source (two unique partial indexes, created `IF NOT EXISTS` on the next boot), plus `retired` ones being deleted. Passage tables are unchanged: they are per vector width and already keyed by generation.
- **`beginBuild`** takes the builder lock, then: same fingerprint as the active one, rebuild in place; same as the one under construction, take it up (resumed with what it holds); otherwise retire any unfinished one and open a new `building` generation numbered past every generation the source has. Orphan passages (generation row deleted by hand) are deleted before any generation opens, as the first generation already did.
- **Writes** go to the generation of the fingerprint they carry: during a build, the walk and event-sync writes carry the new one and land in the new generation only. Each write share-locks its generation row inside its transaction, so a switch or a retirement waits for it, and a write that finds its generation retired is planned again.
- **Search** under the new fingerprint while its generation is building answers `KNOWLEDGE_REBUILD_REQUIRED` (409), message "is being rebuilt" (the same code and wording as knowledge-turso). The ranking statement holds only while its generation is active (an `EXISTS` on the generation row in the same statement), and a search that meets a switch runs again, at most three times; the third answers an error rather than an empty result.
- **`completeBuild`** (the service calls it after the walk and its single purge) retires the active generation and activates the new one in one transaction, then deletes the retired generation's passages in batches of `deleteBatchSize` rows (default 1000) and its row last. A deletion that stops is logged at `warn` and finished by the next build; a retired generation is never read.
- **One builder per source:** a PostgreSQL session advisory lock (key: 64 bits of a hash of schema and source id) held from `beginBuild` to `completeBuild` on a connection outside the pool (`PgPoolLike.connectSession`, provided by `poolFromPg`). A second builder gets `LOCK_CONFLICT` (409, standard catalog), so its walk reads and embeds nothing. Freed on completion, on process or connection death (PostgreSQL), after `buildLockIdleMs` (15 minutes) without a call of the build itself (calls with reason `reindex`; event-sync writes do not hold it), and on plugin `destroy`. It is a session lock, so the store needs a direct or session-mode PostgreSQL connection: a transaction-mode pooler breaks it. When `pg_advisory_unlock` answers false (the session no longer held the lock), the release is logged at `warn` and names that requirement. A crashed build is **resumable**: the next build under the same fingerprint keeps what was written and the walk skips it by document hash.
- **Fresh database.** Two sessions that ran `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector` at the same moment: the loser failed on the catalogue's unique key, and `ready()` refused although the extension existed. It now re-reads the extension after a failed create and refuses only when it is still missing (pre-existing, seen as a flaky first reindex on a fresh database while the live suite ran its files in parallel).
- **New exports, all optional (widening):** adapter options `buildLockIdleMs`, `deleteBatchSize`, `logger`; `PgPoolLike.connectSession`; `PgvectorKnowledgeAdapter.close()`. The changeset stays `patch` and carries the same `Clause-②` line.
- No contract member is added: `beginBuild`, `completeBuild`, `indexStatus.building` and `ctx.index` are ADR-0161 K8 item 8, already on main. No error code is added. `service-knowledge` needs no change: its walk already calls `beginBuild`, purges once and calls `completeBuild`.
- Docs: a "Generations" subsection in `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`, and one bullet in its pgvector section. The "Rebuilds" section of `packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/README.md` (it ships in the npm tarball) and the "Rebuilds" bullet of `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` section 4.1 now describe generations; the hand-run clear-SQL instructions are gone (claim amend 7187694971). All three say the builder lock needs a direct or session-mode connection.

## Tests

- New file `generations.live-postgres.test.ts` (live PostgreSQL + pgvector, the package's existing live pattern): same width with the model changed, through `KnowledgeService` (generation 2 built beside generation 1; search during the build refused "being rebuilt"; an event-sync write during the build lands only in generation 2 and is present after the switch; purge 0; generation 1 deleted; reading `current`). Also: two concurrent builds (one builds, the other gets `LOCK_CONFLICT` and embeds nothing); a build whose session is terminated is resumed by another adapter with its passage kept; the idle release while event-sync writes keep arriving (they do not extend the lock; released after `buildLockIdleMs`); batched deletion (5 rows at batch 2 = 3 statements) and abandoning a generation for a third fingerprint.
- New file `builder-lock.test.ts` (no database): a release whose `pg_advisory_unlock` answers false logs one warning naming the direct or session-mode connection; one that answers true logs nothing.
- Contract suite: `generations: true` for pgvector (it was `false`, pending this card).
- `acceptance.live-postgres.test.ts`: two cases that pinned the retired behaviour (reindex refused with hand-run clear SQL; `beginBuild` under another fingerprint refused) are rewritten to the new behaviour. The case that ran the printed clear SQL is removed, because that SQL is no longer printed. The rebuild-required remedy is pinned to say "complete reindex" and to carry no `DELETE FROM`, `DROP` or `TRUNCATE`.

## Acceptance notes

- Fixed in this PR (dc620cdb6): the README "Rebuilds" section and the protocol section 4.1 "Rebuilds" bullet said the store does not yet build a second generation and printed clear SQL. Both now describe the generations behaviour, after the claim amend added the two files to the surface. Left as is, being generic and still true: protocol section 3.6's sentence about an adapter that does not keep generations.
- The builder lock is held on a dedicated session for the whole build. A walk that fails on a process that keeps running keeps it until `buildLockIdleMs` passes; another process is refused `LOCK_CONFLICT` meanwhile, and that refusal's remedy says when it frees. Fencing a build that lost its lock mid-walk is #37465 (service lease), not this PR.
- Carried, not fixed here (seat note 7188645663): N1 (fencing a builder that lost its lock) goes to #37465. N2, a `building` generation that stays after the fingerprint is reverted to the active one, is deleted at the next build under another fingerprint; until then it holds rows and is never read. N4, two sweeps of the same retired generation at once, can leave passage rows behind when one deletes the generation row first; the sweep no longer sees them (it walks generation rows); they are never read, and the orphan cleanup deletes them when the source next opens a generation. N3 (that third error carries no code): giving it `CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION` (409) pins a code that `scripts/error-status-unpinned-baseline.json` lists as unpinned, and `check:error-status-conformance` then requires that row to be removed. The file is outside the claim surface, so the code was taken back out; it needs a one-line claim amend. Protocol section 9's table row is outside the claim surface and left as is.
- A second builder that took over after an idle release writes the same documents under the same fingerprint into the same generation, so the index stays correct; only embedding spend is doubled.

## Verification

Read first, by risk: `pgvector-adapter.ts` `completeBuild` and `sweepRetired` (the switch and the batched delete), `searchAttempt` (the `EXISTS` guard and the retry), `takeBuilderLock` and `releaseBuilderLock`.

Two-minute check: with `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` pointing at a PostgreSQL that has pgvector, run `pnpm --filter @objectstack/knowledge-pgvector exec vitest run src/__tests__/generations.live-postgres.test.ts`. You should see 5 passed, among them the idle release under event-sync writes and the "model changed" case that is refused "being rebuilt" mid-build.

<details><summary>Local test runs (head 06d53aa71; PostgreSQL 16.16 + pgvector 0.8.7, a local instance, fresh database)</summary>

- Package suite with the live files on, `vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --reporter=verbose` under the verify lock: `Test Files 6 passed (6)`, `Tests 75 passed (75)`, lock VERDICT command-exit 0. All 5 generation cases and both builder-lock cases passed. Run at tree 06d53aa71 (the same tree as d1c735dce, whose commits were reworded only), plus `not-ready.test.ts` 11/11 with the new race case.
- `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build` of the package: exit 0, check-dts-emitted 2/2.
- Correction: the runs reported at bc0cab45f and dc620cdb6 as "pgvector 0.8" were on pgvector 0.6.0. Every run since fb4146c9b is on 0.8.7, the version the CI live job uses.
</details>

<details><summary>Ablations (each restored, git diff empty afterwards)</summary>

- A: writes no longer go to the generation under construction. Red: 3 failed of 5 (model changed; session died and resumed; batches and third fingerprint).
- B: the advisory lock answer is ignored. Red: 2 failed of 5 (two concurrent builds; idle release).
- C: one delete batch only. Red: 1 failed of 5 (batched deletion).
- D (round 3): event-sync calls touch the lock again (`reason` check removed). Red: 1 failed of 5, the idle release while event-sync writes arrive.
- E (round 3): no re-read after a failed CREATE EXTENSION. Red: 1 failed of 11 in `not-ready.test.ts`, the lost-race case.
</details>

<details><summary>Derived gates (dispatch-gates, 102 families over the whole change)</summary>

`--ran` reconciliation at 06d53aa71: 102 derived, 100 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED, 0 unrun. The two are PREREQUISITE NOT MET (exit 3) on this checkout: `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` (shallow clone) and `spec check:skill-examples` (client-react not built). This round ran 98 families for the round-3 paths, then 61 again for the adapter and changeset after the last code change, and 6 more for `not-ready.test.ts`. One went red in between: `check:error-status-conformance`, which N3's `CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION` tripped (see Acceptance notes). It is green after that code was taken out. `overlap-check`: clean against origin/main 54ea3c8c3, #37477 and #37442. PR check-runs at 06d53aa71: 53 completed, 38 success, 15 skipped, 0 failure. The CI check-runs are the authority. The live pgvector job (`Temporal Conformance`) runs in the merge queue, not on the PR.
</details>
